articles.title: PM Modi Jhalmuri break: Security stepped up at stall which Modi had visited in West Bengal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bikram Kumar Sau, a Jhalmuri vendor in Jhargram town, West Bengal, has reported receiving threatening phone calls and messages after Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited his stall during the state assembly election campaign.  The Jhargram police have launched an investigation into the threats, with security personnel posted outside the stall to protect Sau and his family. The incident gained national attention and contributed to the BJP's victory in the district.

articles.title: What did the Supreme Court say about bail under UAPA? - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court granted six months of interim bail to two accused in the 2020 Delhi riots case, Abdul Khalid Saifi and Tasleem Ahmad. The court also referred a larger bench to consider whether prolonged incarceration and delays in trials can override stringent bail restrictions under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967.

articles.title: West Bengal gained infamy due to recruitment scams, new recruitment policy in next Budget session: CM - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Suvendu Adhikari, West Bengal Chief Minister, announced a new recruitment policy for the state during the Rojgar Mela in Sealdah. The policy will be introduced in the next Budget session of the assembly, beginning on June 18th.  Adhikari cited previous recruitment scams under the Trinamool Congress regime, including teacher and municipal job scandals, as reasons for the new policy. He also expressed concerns about the lack of transparency in examinations and suggested a carbon copy of the OMR sheet be given to all examinees to prevent nepotism and corruption.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The article highlights ongoing recruitment scams and their impact on citizens.

articles.title: Centre asks Delhi Gymkhana Club to hand over premises by June 5 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Union Urban Affairs Ministry has ordered the Delhi Gymkhana Club, located adjacent to the Prime Minister's residence, to vacate its premises by June 5th. The club's 27.3-acre plot is needed for "strengthening and securing defense infrastructure" and other vital public security purposes.  The order was issued by the Land & Development Office (L&DO) under the Union Housing and Urban Affairs Ministry, citing urgent institutional needs and governance infrastructure projects as reasons. The club has operated from the location since 1913.

articles.title: Future City will serve as compass for the country: TPCC chief - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mahesh Goud, president of the Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC), criticized T. Harish Rao, a BRS MLA, for his comments on the future development of Hyderabad.  Goud argued that expanding the city's geographical limits was necessary for state development and questioned Harish Rao’s lack of foresight. He also stated that the Congress government is continuing previous schemes and working towards announcing names for working presidents soon.

articles.title: Pinarayi flays crackdown on Cockroach Janta Party - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Pinarayi Vijayan, leader of the Opposition, criticized the Union government's withholding of the Cockroach Janta Party’s X handle. He argued that this action reflects intolerance towards democratic protests and suggests fear of the youth movement becoming a political force.  Vijayan stated that the platform has gained significant traction due to its focus on addressing unemployment and inequality, highlighting the deep discontent among young people.

articles.title: Congress slams Centre over rising fuel prices, questions PM for not disclosing seriousness of crisis - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress leaders criticized the Prime Minister Narendra Modi government for its handling of rising fuel prices, accusing it of "looting" consumers with high taxes and failing to pass on benefits during periods of low global crude prices.  Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge accused the government of timing fuel price reductions around elections and resuming hikes after polling concluded. Rajeev Gowda, a Congress research department chairman, argued that rising fuel prices and the depreciating rupee reflected broader economic distress and called for greater transparency from the government regarding its energy policies.

articles.title: U.P. Congress chief Ajay Rai booked over ‘objectionable’ comment on PM Modi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ajay Rai, Uttar Pradesh Congress president, is facing an FIR after a complaint from Neeraj Kumar Rawat, a BJP district working committee member, alleging abusive remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi.  The complaint claims that Mr. Rai obstructed government work and blocked a public road with his convoy of vehicles and supporters. The police registered the case based on a video circulating online showing Mr. Rai making objectionable statements. Mr. Rai denies the allegations, calling it a tactic to silence him and accusing the BJP government of using state apparatus against opponents.

articles.title: KSRTC driver suspended over defamatory post against Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: KSRTC driver S. Sunilkumar has been suspended for posting defamatory content about Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on Facebook and circulating his picture in a defamatory manner. The corporation initiated disciplinary action against him, while the police are considering filing an IT Act case.  Further investigation is underway with the assistance of the cyber cell.

articles.title: Centre committed to ensuring transparent, corruption-free recruitmentm says Union Minister Joshi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Pralhad Joshi, Union Minister for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution,  emphasized the Centre's commitment to transparent recruitment processes during a Rozgar Mela in Hubballi. He urged newly appointed candidates to serve with integrity and dedication, highlighting Prime Minister Narendra Modi's "Rozgar Parva" initiative which aims to create employment opportunities across India. Over 51,000 candidates received appointment letters from various departments including Railways, banking, and postal services.

articles.title: I don’t think the ruling party has the stomach for sarcasm, says Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a youth-led satirical political group, had its website taken down on Saturday, May 23, 2026 at 9 a.m.  Founder Abhijeet Dipke accused the Indian Government of orchestrating the takedown, claiming it was due to the CJP's growing popularity and online movement demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan following the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak. The CJP, formed in response to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s controversial “cockroach” remark, rapidly gained traction with over 22 million followers on social media before being blocked by authorities citing national security concerns. Dipke claims his personal accounts were also hacked and he has received death threats.  Despite the takedown, the CJP is not yet a registered political party.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Government censorship of a satirical group raises concerns about free speech.

articles.title: TVK government will fall one day, says M.K. Stalin - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M.K. Stalin, leader of the DMK, criticized the TVK government, led by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, for its dependence on other parties for support and alleged attempts to split the AIADMK.  He compared the public's interest in the new party to a child's fascination with a toy, predicting that it would fade quickly. Stalin also highlighted his government's achievements over the past five years as evidence of improved governance.

articles.title: DMK, Congress trade barbs over the latter’s post-poll alliance with the TVK - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: DMK leader Udhayanidhi Stalin accused the Congress of being responsible for the BJP's victories, claiming they had "shed blood and tears" to ensure Congress wins.  DMK president M.K. Stalin was also present at the meeting where a resolution condemned the Congress for its betrayal and labeled it a "parasite".  The Congress Legislature Party leader S. Rajesh Kumar countered these accusations, stating that the people of Tamil Nadu elected the AIADMK to power based on the promise of sharing power with alliance partners.

articles.title: Coalition government here to stay in Tamil Nadu like Kerala, says Kader Mohideen - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K.M. Kader Mohideen, president of the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML), stated that Tamil Nadu has formed a coalition government similar to Kerala and that it will continue in the future. He attributed this success to the DMK's ability to secure votes from the Muslim community, which he believes was crucial for their victory.  C. Joseph Vijay, the new leader of Tamil Nadu politics, is credited with initiating this change.

articles.title: Thousands march in Madrid demanding Spanish PM quit over graft allegations | Protests News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Thousands of people marched in Madrid demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez over corruption allegations. The protest, organized by civic associations and backed by political parties including the Popular Party (PP) and far-right Vox, was sparked by a series of scandals involving Sanchez's family and entourage.  Sanchez has maintained that the accusations are politically motivated, while his brother is scheduled to stand trial for influence peddling and his wife is under investigation in a separate case.

articles.title: Trump's justice department scrubs its website of news releases about January 6 defendants | US Capitol attack | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Department of Justice has removed news releases about criminal cases related to the January 6th Capitol attack, calling the information "partisan propaganda."  Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche has not ruled out compensation for those convicted of crimes during the assault, prompting bipartisan anger in Congress. The department claims it is reversing the weaponization of its website under the Biden administration and will make whole those persecuted for political purposes.

articles.title: DO NOT INVITE: Why Donald Trump offboarded Tulsi Gabbard | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Tulsi Gabbard, former Democratic Congresswoman and Director of National Intelligence, resigned from her position after facing pressure from the Trump administration. Her departure, which followed other high-profile resignations within the Trump Cabinet, was attributed to a lack of trust and alignment with the president's foreign policy decisions.  Gabbard had been criticized for her anti-war stance and perceived disconnect from Trump's actions in Iran and Venezuela. The rise and fall of Gabbard exemplifies the challenges faced by women in positions of power within the Trump administration, where loyalty is often tested by performance and public perception.

articles.title: ‘Don’t mind being called tyrant dictator, but don’t want to be called dumb’: Donald Trump - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump defended his cognitive abilities and intelligence during a rally in New York, dismissing criticism of his mental fitness. He claimed to have passed a cognitive assessment and stated he is the "smartest guy you'll ever meet."  The event also focused on supporting Mike Lawler, a Republican congressman representing a district won by Democrat Kamala Harris, and promoting the expansion of the federal deduction for state and local taxes (SALT).

articles.title: New breed of political prisoner arises in Britain as anti-protest sentences rise | UK criminal justice | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Queen Mary University of London (QMUL) and the protest group Defend Our Juries report that custodial sentences for climate and Palestine-solidarity activists have increased in frequency and length. The research, which will be launched on Tuesday, identifies 286 cases involving 136 years of jail time for protesters who engaged in direct action or civil disobedience. Researchers found that remand detentions are used as a "first line of attack" to deter protest and civil disobedience, with final sentences often more lenient than pre-trial detention.  The report highlights the use of contempt of court charges by private companies and public authorities to jail protesters.

articles.title: India’s government orders handover of exclusive Delhi Gymkhana Club | India | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian government has ordered the Delhi Gymkhana Club, a prestigious private club, to vacate its premises by June 5th. The ministry of housing and urban affairs cited public interest requirements for defense and security infrastructure as justification for the eviction.  This move comes amidst a broader political shift by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who has sought to challenge traditional elites and reshape India's colonial past. The club, founded in 1913, has long been associated with the rich and famous but has faced internal disputes and allegations of financial mismanagement in recent years.

articles.title: One more Trinamool councillor from Bidhannagar arrested - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: TMC councillors from the municipality of Bidhannagar, West Bengal, have been arrested in recent days for charges including intimidation, violence, extortion, and money laundering.  The arrests follow a crackdown by the new BJP government after the 2021 Assembly election. Several other TMC leaders, including a local union leader and a former minister, have also been arrested on various charges. The arrests come amid allegations of post-poll violence and threats against citizens.

articles.title: Democratic chair faces calls to quit over ‘shambles’ of election autopsy release | Democrats | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ken Martin, chair of the Democratic National Committee (DNC), faces calls to resign following the release of a flawed autopsy report on the 2024 presidential election. The report, which omitted key information and lacked oversight, has deepened concerns about Martin's leadership and sparked criticism from Democratic members of Congress and party leaders.  Several voices have called for his resignation, including Seth Moulton, Marc Veasey, and Mark Pocan.  Norm Solomon and Amanda Litman also expressed their dissatisfaction with the report and Martin's handling of it. The Progressive Change Campaign Committee (PCCC) has launched a campaign to pressure state chairs to call for Martin's resignation, while others have suggested potential successors like Jane Kleeb and Ben Wikler.

articles.title: Back Rahul Gandhi’s call for ‘Samvidhan Bachao’, says Jagga Reddy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: T. Jagga Reddy, a senior Congress leader, defended Rahul Gandhi's "Samvidhan Bachao" campaign, arguing that the Constitution and democratic values are under threat under the current BJP-led government. He compared the Constitution to Karna's armor in the Mahabharata, stating that its protection is vital for citizens' rights and freedoms.  He called for vigilance to safeguard voting rights and constitutional freedoms, highlighting Congress contributions to India's democratic systems throughout history.

articles.title: Chief Electoral Officer (Kerala) Rathan U. Kelkar appointed Secretary to Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rathan U. Kelkar, the Chief Electoral Officer of Kerala, will transition from his role to become the Secretary to Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan.  Mr. Kelkar, a 2003 batch IAS officer, has been in the news for overseeing the recent Kerala Assembly elections and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The appointment follows the recent appointment of Manoj Kumar Agarwal as Chief Secretary to the new BJP government in West Bengal.  The State government will send a panel of names to the Election Commission to appoint a new CEO once Mr. Kelkar is relieved of his duties.

articles.title: Reeves begins push to remain as chancellor under new Labour leadership | Rachel Reeves | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Rachel Reeves, the UK chancellor, is facing pressure to stay in her position despite calls for a new leader within Labour.  Her supporters argue that she is the best candidate to maintain financial stability and reassure markets. However, concerns remain about her ability to address the new economic challenges posed by the Iran war and potential changes under a new prime minister, particularly given the possibility of Andy Burnham replacing Keir Starmer. Reeves has been actively lobbying MPs to support her candidacy, but some Labour MPs are critical of her handling of issues like winter fuel payments and disability benefits.  The future of the chancellor's job remains uncertain as she navigates these internal challenges.

articles.title: Senegal President Faye sacks prime minister Sonko after months or tensions
articles.rephrased_article: President Bassirou Diomaye Faye of Senegal has dismissed Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko and dissolved the government, citing months of tensions between them. The decree followed a parliamentary session where Sonko criticized Faye.  The move comes amid mounting economic pressure in the country, with its public debt exceeding 132% of GDP. Sonko, who enjoys widespread popularity among young Senegalese, has vowed to "sleep with a light heart" despite the dismissal.

articles.title: Anthony Albanese visibly emotional after defending Labor’s capital gains tax and negative gearing changes | Australian politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Anthony Albanese, the prime minister, defended his government's proposed changes to negative gearing, capital gains tax (CGT), and family trusts. He argued that these reforms are necessary to rebalance the housing market in favor of first-time home buyers and ensure a fairer system for working Australians.  Albanese emphasized that Labor is committed to supporting aspiration for all, including young people who struggle to enter the housing market. While some Labor MPs expressed concerns about the potential negative impact on property investors, Chris Bowen, the energy minister, stated that these changes are crucial for intergenerational equity and acknowledged that they may be controversial but ultimately beneficial.  The opposition leader, Angus Taylor, criticized the budget as an attack on young Australians and a threat to their aspirations.

articles.title: Ponraj gets anticipatory bail over remarks on TVK women supporters - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V. Ponraj, a political commentator, has been granted anticipatory bail by the Madras High Court in two criminal cases related to derogatory remarks against women supporters of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK). The court imposed conditions requiring him to appear before police twice a week and once a week, as well as refrain from threatening witnesses or tampering with evidence.  The judge acknowledged the intent behind Ponraj's statements but granted bail due to his strong ties to society and low risk of absconding.

articles.title: Delhi HC seeks response from AAP’s Gopal Rai, journalist in contempt plea - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Gopal Rai, an AAP leader, and journalist Saurav Das were issued notices by the Delhi High Court in response to a petition seeking contempt proceedings against them for allegedly orchestrating a social media campaign against Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma. The petition also named former Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal and ex-AAP MLA Saurabh Bhardwaj as parties, alleging that they exerted extra-judicial pressure on the judge through their social media posts.  The court has listed the case for further hearing on August 4th after observing that a contempt case is already underway against Kejriwal and others.

articles.title: Meet demands or face budget boycott, Achakzai tells govt - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Mehmood Khan Achakzai, leader of the opposition in the National Assembly, warned Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif that the upcoming budget session would be a complete boycott if the government does not meet their demands for Imran Khan's medical treatment and unrestricted visitation rights.  He also criticized the lackluster attendance from the treasury benches as evidence of the government's disregard for parliament. Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, chairman of the PTI, accused the government of suppressing dissent and police excesses against those attempting to visit Imran Khan in prison.

articles.title: Race for French presidency sees ex-PM Philippe as early favourite to beat populists
articles.rephrased_article: Edouard Philippe, the former prime minister of Emmanuel Macron, is emerging as the frontrunner in the French presidential race.  He is seen as the only candidate capable of defeating a hard-right candidate, such as Marine Le Pen, or her deputy Jordan Bardella.  Philippe's campaign strategy focuses on appealing to center-right voters and positioning himself as a barrier against far-right populism. However, challenges remain, including potential rivalries within the center-right, the ongoing corruption probe into Philippe, and the unpredictable nature of the political landscape. The outcome of the race will likely hinge on the performance of Marine Le Pen and her party, the National Rally (RN), as well as the strength of the hard-left candidate, Jean-Luc Mélenchon.

articles.title: Centre promised more legislative powers for Ladakh, says delegation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) proposed a new mechanism to grant Ladakh greater legislative, financial, and administrative powers within the existing Union Territory framework.  Civil society members who attended a sub-committee meeting with MHA officials on Friday (May 22, 2026) reported that the talks were positive and that the MHA would soon send a draft outlining the proposed changes.

articles.title: Seven MLAs from Chennai find place in Tamil Nadu cabinet: highest in recent years - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and seven other ministers from Chennai constituencies were sworn in on Thursday, marking a significant representation for the city in the new cabinet.  This is one of the highest contributions to the current cabinet from Chennai, with many top leaders from the Tamil Nadu Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) contesting from the city and becoming ministers.

articles.title: Bengali actors face heat after power shift to BJP; FIR filed over 2021 social media posts linked to post-poll violence - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Parambrata Chatterjee, a Bengali actor, announced he had to align with the Trinamool Congress after the recent West Bengal Assembly election results.  He stated this decision was made for his one-year-old son, prompting strong reactions from social media users and fellow actors. Keya Ghosh, a BJP leader, responded by criticizing Chatterjee's compromise and highlighting the unwavering support of many BJP supporters in the state.

articles.title: The turbulent 15 months of Trump’s unlikely US intelligence director | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Tulsi Gabbard, the former Democrat and former Hawaii representative, resigned as director of national intelligence on Friday.  Her tenure was marked by tension with President Donald Trump, who often excluded her from key conversations and publicly questioned her intelligence assessments. Despite efforts to streamline the agency, Gabbard's relationship with the president deteriorated over time, culminating in a public disagreement about Iran and a perceived partisan approach to her role. Following Gabbard's resignation, Aaron Lukas will serve as acting director until June 30th.

articles.title: Elected government has no role in Jammu demolitions, says Farooq Abdullah - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Farooq Abdullah, president of the National Conference (NC), stated that the elected government has no involvement in the ongoing demolitions in Jammu.  He accused the opposition parties of pursuing anti-Gujjar policies and claimed that Gujjars and Bakerwals have historically protected the region's borders. Gulam Ali Khatana, a BJP Rajya Sabha member, countered by accusing the NC and Congress of neglecting the development of Gujjar and Pahari communities for decades. He praised the Modi government's efforts to empower these communities.

articles.title: Tulsi Gabbard resigns as Trump’s top US intelligence official | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Tulsi Gabbard, former Democratic congresswoman and presidential candidate, resigned as Donald Trump's director of national intelligence citing her husband's recent diagnosis with a rare form of bone cancer.  She cited her decision to leave the administration in part due to her opposition to US military interventionism, which she has held since serving in the Hawaii National Guard during the Iraq War. The president confirmed Gabbard's resignation and appointed Aaron Lukas as acting director.

articles.title: Protester with ‘Trump is a war criminal’ banner removed from Trump rally in New York state – US politics live | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump held a rally in Rockland county, New York, where he was interrupted twice by protesters. The president then spoke about how his supporters had previously defended him from protestors and claimed that the recent disruptions were "dangerous." Trump also addressed the case of Kilmar Ábrego García, who was deported to El Salvador despite a US court order barring it. He blamed the previous administration for sending Ábrego to the prison, claiming an "administrative error".  The president then spoke about his son's upcoming wedding and claimed that he had been forced to return to Washington due to government matters. Trump boasted about passing a dementia test and recounted a story about a friend who complained about the cost of GLP-1 shots. He also announced Aaron Lukas as acting director of national intelligence after Tulsi Gabbard resigned.

articles.title: Burnham says politics ‘needs new script’ and vows to change Labour if elected as Makerfield MP – as it happened | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Andy Burnham launched his campaign as the Labour candidate in the Makerfield byelection. He stated that a vote for him is a vote to change Labour and highlighted successes of Greater Manchester and Liverpool since he left Westminster in 2017. The Green party's candidate, Chris Kennedy, withdrew from the ballot just nine hours after being announced.  John Healey, the defence secretary, urged Nigel Farage to provide transparency about a £5 million gift he received from a billionaire businessman.  The UK borrowed more than expected in April due to high inflation, and the Office for National Statistics reported public sector net borrowing of £24.3 billion.

articles.title: Wes Streeting insists he can win Labour leadership race despite ‘underdog’ status | Wes Streeting | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Wes Streeting, former health secretary, launched a shadow campaign for the Labour leadership, arguing that Keir Starmer is unfit to lead.  He believes he can win over Labour members despite trailing in polls and being seen as right-leaning. Streeting outlined plans including moving families out of temporary accommodation, speeding up the establishment of a national care service, and introducing a wealth tax. He also suggested bringing back environmental impact assessments for large developments and addressing concerns about immigration.  Andy Burnham, who is campaigning to win a byelection in Makerfield, is seen as Streeting's main rival.

articles.title: Slovenia’s parliament approves right-wing Janez Jansa as prime minister | Government News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Slovenia’s parliament voted to approve Janez Jansa, a right-wing populist, as prime minister.  Jansa's appointment follows a post-election stalemate and marks a shift from the country's previous liberal government. The new coalition government, formed by Jansa’s Slovenian Democratic Party (SDS) and several center-right groups, will hold 43 seats in the assembly. Jansa has previously served as prime minister from 2004 to 2008, 2012 to 2013, and 2020 to 2022.  He plans to prioritize economic growth, fighting corruption, and decentralization.

articles.title: Carney says Alberta is 'essential' to Canada as province plans vote on separation
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Mark Carney stated that Alberta is an "essential" part of Canada, while Alberta Premier Danielle Smith announced a referendum on October 19th to determine whether the province should remain in Canada or pursue independence. The vote comes after pressure from a growing separatist movement and a recent legal challenge by First Nations groups halted the process of verifying petition signatures.  Smith maintains that Albertans deserve a say in their future, despite criticism from various organizations, including the Sturgeon Lake Cree Nation and the New Democratic Party.

articles.title: PTI workers stage protests in various cities, defy Section 144 in Islamabad - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: PTI and TTAP organized protests across Pakistan on Friday, demanding the release of former prime minister Imran Khan and addressing concerns over inflation, rising petroleum prices, and deteriorating law and order.  PTI Islamabad President Aamir Mughal, along with other leaders, held a protest in Islamabad despite Section 144 being in place, while Shandana Gulzar from TTAP spoke at a press conference in Peshawar, highlighting the plight of civilians in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and accusing the federal government of mismanagement. These protests were joined by political and social activists across the country, including those from the Haqooq-i-Khalq Party.

articles.title: Tulsi Gabbard resigns as US director of national intelligence
articles.rephrased_article: Tulsi Gabbard, the US director of national intelligence under President Donald Trump, will resign from her position on June 30th.  She cited her husband's recent bone cancer diagnosis as the reason for her departure, stating she cannot continue in her role while he faces this challenge. Trump expressed his support for Gabbard and noted her "incredible job" during her tenure.  Aaron Lukas, the principal deputy director, will assume the acting director position.

articles.title: Canada’s Carney says Alberta is ‘essential’ as province mulls separation | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney emphasized the importance of Alberta to Canada's economy, stating that he is working with the province to improve it.  Premier Danielle Smith announced a referendum on whether Alberta should remain part of Canada or hold a vote for separation. The decision came after a court blocked a petition to hold a vote on separation, citing lack of consultation with Indigenous groups. Smith stated she opposes separation but believes in respecting the democratic rights of Albertans and that she will respect the results of the referendum.  Conservative Party Leader Pierre Poilievre said he would campaign against separation, while some Liberals criticized Smith for stoking separatist sentiment for political gains.

articles.title: Canadian prime minister says Alberta ‘essential’ to country as separatists push for independence | Canada | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Mark Carney, the Canadian prime minister, emphasized that Alberta is crucial to Canada's future.  Following a judge's ruling halting an independence referendum petition, Danielle Smith, Alberta's premier, vowed to hold a vote on whether to initiate the legal process for a binding referendum in October. Smith maintains she supports Alberta remaining within Canada but believes a public debate is necessary.  Carney expressed support for Canada and its future while acknowledging that Alberta plays a vital role.

articles.title: Turkish opposition fights court ousting of leaders in ruling boosting Erdogan
articles.rephrased_article: The Turkish opposition, led by Özgür Özel of the Republican People's Party (CHP), is challenging a court ruling removing them from leadership positions. The appeals court declared the 2023 leadership election null and void, prompting protests and criticism from opposition leaders who accuse President Recep Tayyip Erdogan of seeking to eliminate rivals.  The ruling has sparked concerns about the future of Turkey's political landscape and potential for snap elections.

articles.title: Tony Abbott to become new Liberal party president in former PM’s return to political frontlines | Tony Abbott | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Tony Abbott, the former Australian prime minister, will become the new president of the Liberal party.  He was unanimously elected after his sole opponent, former foreign minister Alexander Downer, chose to run for vice-president. The election will be confirmed at the Liberal party's federal council meeting next weekend. Abbott will succeed John Olsen and return to active politics after losing his seat in 2019.  Moderate Liberals are concerned about Abbott's potential influence on party direction, particularly regarding immigration. Meanwhile, the Victorian Liberal party state council is holding a meeting where former federal director Brian Loughnane, who is married to Peta Credlin, is expected to be elected as president.

articles.title: After CM Vijay’s order to revive Amma Canteens, AIADMK hopes for comeback of other legacy schemes - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: AIADMK functionaries have called for the revival and strengthening of several welfare schemes implemented during the party's previous tenures, including Amma Canteens, Amma Salt, Cradle Baby scheme, Amma Scooters, and 'Gold for Thali'. They also criticized the Tamil Nadu government's handling of government properties and alleged that several welfare programs initiated by the previous AIADMK regime have been discontinued or poorly implemented.  These criticisms were made during a meeting with the newly elected government led by C. Joseph Vijay.

articles.title: Turkish court ousts leader of main opposition party | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A Turkish court overturned the 2023 leadership election of the main opposition Republican People’s Party (CHP), reinstating former chair Kemal Kilicdaroglu as interim leader. The ruling is seen as a move against the CHP, which won a significant victory over President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's AK Party in the 2024 local elections and has been rising in polls. The CHP rejected the decision as an "attempted coup," while the government claimed it renewed faith in the rule of law.  The ruling sparked market turmoil, with the Borsa Istanbul index dropping 6 percent and government bonds sliding.

articles.title: Congress leader Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan elected Kerala Speaker - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Thiruvanchoor Radhakrishnan, a senior Congress leader, was elected as the Speaker of the 16th Kerala Legislative Assembly on Friday (May 22, 2026). He won with 101 votes, defeating A.C. Moideen and B.B. Gopakumar.  The election took place after G. Sudhakaran, the previous Pro Tem Speaker, chose not to vote.  V.D. Satheesan, the Chief Minister, and Pinarayi Vijayan, the Leader of the Opposition, led Radhakrishnan to the Speaker's chair.

articles.title: DMK faces a challenge as allies set to join TVK government - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: DMK, the Secular Progressive Alliance's leader since 2017, has lost most of its pre-poll allies.  The party is now left with only MDMK and Manithaneya Makkal Katchi, who contested on its Rising Sun symbol. Additionally, the DMDK remains loyal to the TVK government. The Congress abandoned the DMK after the Assembly polls and joined Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay's Cabinet on Thursday, while the IUML and VCK are expected to join the Ministry on Friday.

articles.title: Voter confusion fears over simultaneous polls ‘misplaced’, says ONOE JPC chairman - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: P.P. Chaudhary, chairman of the Joint Parliamentary Committee on ‘One Nation One Election’, defended the proposal, arguing that Indian voters are politically astute and can differentiate between national and state issues.  He cited examples from Delhi and other states where voters supported different parties in Lok Sabha and Assembly elections. CII, ASSOCHAM, and GCCI backed the proposal, while Gujarat University Vice-Chancellor Dr. Neerja Gupta highlighted how frequent polls disrupt academic schedules and increase financial costs. The committee also heard concerns from the Congress, which argued that simultaneous elections would allow national narratives to overshadow state issues.

articles.title: House Republicans cancel vote on war powers resolution to end US war in Iran | House of Representatives | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: House Republicans canceled a scheduled vote on a war powers resolution aimed at ending the US war with Iran, avoiding potential political embarrassment for Donald Trump.  The cancellation prompted criticism from Hakeem Jeffries, Katherine Clark, and Pete Aguilar, who called it cowardly. The Democrats argued that the Republican-controlled House is acting as a "wholly-owned subsidiary" of the Trump administration. Despite the postponement until June, the resolution is expected to pass with bipartisan support.

articles.title: Trump is supporting Spencer Pratt in the LA mayor’s race. It may be a poison pill | Los Angeles | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump's recent endorsement of Spencer Pratt, a former Republican and reality TV star, is expected to benefit Democrats in the Los Angeles mayoral race.  Pratt has gained traction by capitalizing on anger over the city's response to the wildfires and homelessness crisis. While Pratt claims his focus will be solely on local issues, his opponents have seized on Trump's support as a sign of potential conservative leanings.

articles.title: US Senate pushes back against Trump’s $1.8bn ‘anti-weaponisation’ fund | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Senate Republicans delayed a vote on immigration enforcement funding, citing concerns about President Donald Trump’s “anti-weaponisation” fund and his request for $1 billion in funds to build a White House ballroom.  The delay comes after Trump sued the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) for leaking his tax refunds, prompting criticism of potential conflicts of interest.  Senator Don Bacon stated that Trump has lost support within the Senate due to these actions, and Senator Thom Tillis called the “anti-weaponisation” fund "stupid on stilts." The Senate will return from its recess in June.

articles.title: Historic shift: Vijay’s Cabinet marks Tamil Nadu’s best SC representation till date - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, has appointed seven members from the Scheduled Caste (SC) community to his Cabinet. This marks a significant increase in SC representation compared to previous Cabinets.  Political analyst Stalin Rajangam believes this is a positive step towards inclusivity and sets a benchmark for future governments. However, Punitha Pandiyan, former Vice President of the Tamil Nadu SC/ST Commission, argues that celebrating this development trivializes SC politics.

articles.title: 22 Ministers aged below 50: Cabinet signals generational shift in Tamil Nadu politics - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tamil Nadu government's Cabinet has seen a significant shift in age composition, with the 2026 TVK Cabinet featuring the youngest average age among the three governments examined.  C. Joseph Vijay, the Chief Minister of this government, is 51 years old and his cabinet features the youngest Ministers at just 28 and 29 years old. The 2026 TVK Cabinet has nine Ministers in their 30s, followed by a senior tier of seven Ministers in their 50s, three in their 60s, and only one in the 70-80 age bracket.  This contrasts with the 2021 DMK Cabinet which was heavily dominated by older leaders.

articles.title: Congress workers clash with police in Jaipur during stir against NEET-UG paper leak - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress party workers clashed with police in Rajasthan on Thursday during a protest against the NEET-UG exam paper leak.  Led by State Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra, the protesters demanded the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and the dissolution of the National Testing Agency. The demonstrators, carrying banners and placards, were forcibly dispersed using water cannons. Some protesters suffered minor injuries.

articles.title: BJP functionary’s request to HR&CE Minister - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vinoj Selvam, a BJP functionary, urged newly appointed Ramesh, the Minister for Hindu Religious & Charitable Endowments, to only worship at the Srirangam temple if he visits.  Selvam's statement followed social media posts showing Ramesh with images of late social reformer 'Periyar' E.V. Ramasamy.

articles.title: Ladakh seeks belonging through representation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Union Ministry of Home Affairs argues that Ladakh needs more districts rather than a legislature due to its sparse population, strategic sensitivity, and financial dependence on the Centre. This argument is criticized as flawed and reflects an impoverished understanding of democracy, echoing historical paternalistic views by the British Empire.

articles.title: Ladakh leaders to meet Home Ministry officials on May 22, Sonam Wangchuk part of delegation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A delegation from Ladakh, including climate activist Sonam Wangchuk, is meeting with Union Home Ministry officials on Friday to discuss demands for constitutional safeguards such as Statehood and inclusion under the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution. This meeting follows a previous inconclusive high-powered committee meeting in February and comes after the violence in Leh city in September 2025, which stalled talks.  The delegation will reiterate their demands for Statehood, while officials have offered safeguards under Article 371 of the Constitution.

articles.title: Imran’s cases will be fixed after Eid, CJP assures PTI - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Justice of Pakistan (CJP) Yahya Afridi assured PTI General Secretary Salman Akram Raja that the cases concerning access to a personal physician, family members and counsel for former premier Imran Khan would be scheduled after Eidul Azha.  Raja reported that the CJP had issued instructions to senior officers of the Supreme Court to fix these petitions. The PTI general secretary also stated that the appeals regarding Imran's access were pending before the SC since October 2025, and a petition by Imran's sister challenging the IHC ruling was also pending.  The Supreme Court disposed of appeals filed by the Punjab prosecution seeking cancellation of bail granted to Ejaz Ahmed Chaudhry, involved in the May 9 cases.

articles.title: Take forward reforms, PM tells Ministers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi convened a full Council of Ministers meeting in New Delhi on Thursday, May 21, 2026. The session focused on the government's reform agenda amidst geopolitical shifts and saw presentations from various ministries including labor, power, commerce, finance, agriculture, railways, and NITI Aayog.  The meetings reviewed past achievements and future plans, outlining targets for each ministry.

articles.title: David Lammy chairs first meeting of board set up to improve diversity among judiciary | Judiciary | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: David Lammy, the first black lord chancellor, and Sue Carr, the lady chief justice, have formed a new judicial and legal diversity board to address underrepresentation of minority ethnic and working-class solicitors in the judiciary. The board aims to fast-track solicitor recruitment from underrepresented backgrounds and improve mentoring schemes for new recruits.  The initiative follows criticism that Lammy's plans to reduce jury trials could exacerbate racial and class bias within the judiciary, a concern echoed by legal professionals like Keir Monteith KC who believe institutional racism hinders progress. The board hopes to work with existing organizations like the UK Association of Black Judges to address these issues.

articles.title: Himachal urban poll results reflect public confidence in Congress; party united with no groupism, says CM Sukhu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh, attributed the Congress-backed candidates' victory in recent urban local body elections to public approval of the party's governance. He highlighted the sustained popularity despite anti-incumbency pressures and emphasized a unified effort among party workers.  He also criticized the BJP for its perceived lack of support for Himachal Pradesh, particularly regarding issues like the Revenue Deficit Grant and natural disasters. Sukhu asserted that the Congress has fulfilled its promises and exceeded expectations in delivering on commitments such as welfare schemes and reforms in education and healthcare.

articles.title: Sedition trials can go on if accused is willing: Supreme Court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court has lifted a four-year hold on sedition trials, allowing courts to proceed with cases where the accused do not object. The court clarified that if an accused consents to continued proceedings under Section 124A of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), courts can decide matters on merits. This decision follows an interim order in 2022, during which the court had requested the government to reconsider the colonial-era provision.  The Supreme Court directed the Madhya Pradesh High Court to hear the petitioner's appeal and related cases.

articles.title: Parody Cockroach Janta political party’s rise reflects youth anger in India | India | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A satirical online movement, the Cockroach Janta (People's) party, has gained significant traction in India.  Abhijeet Dipke, a political communications strategist and student at Boston University, founded the movement after Surya Kant, the Supreme Court chief justice, sparked backlash with comments comparing unemployed young people to cockroaches. The CJP uses absurdist humor to mock corruption, joblessness, and government dysfunction, attracting millions of followers on social media.  While some dismiss it as a digital gimmick, Dipke believes it reflects mounting frustration among India's youth and could lead to real political change.

articles.title: From rallies to reels: political catchphrases turn dance anthems in Kolkata - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A new genre of political techno remixes has emerged in Kolkata, using catchy hooks and meme-friendly punchlines to criticize politicians. The trend began with songs like "Khela Hobe" and continues with remixed versions of "Hamba Hamba", "Mach Chor", and "File Chor". These songs often target specific individuals or parties, gaining popularity through social media platforms like Instagram and YouTube Shorts.  The use of crude humor and satirical lyrics reflects a culture of insult-flinging on social media while also expressing anger towards political leaders who abuse power.

articles.title: India's 'Cockroach Janta Party' goes viral, spotlights Gen Z worries - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A five-day-old group called the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has gained significant traction in India, surpassing the Instagram followers of the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).  The CJP, founded by 30-year-old Abhijeet Dipke, addresses issues like unemployment, inflation, and political representation, resonating with a large segment of young Indians who feel ignored by mainstream politics. The group's rapid growth reflects the anxieties felt by India's youth, as highlighted in a recent Deloitte Global survey that found Gen Z facing financial stress and postponing major life decisions due to economic concerns. Dipke emphasizes the CJP's commitment to democratic and peaceful means of political engagement, while also acknowledging its potential for significant change within Indian politics.

articles.title: Five key takeaways from Democrats’ autopsy report on Kamala Harris’s loss | Kamala Harris News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Democratic National Committee (DNC) released its long-awaited autopsy report on why former Vice President Kamala Harris lost the 2024 presidential election. The report, riddled with factual errors and missing sections, failed to address key issues like the Biden administration's support for Israel during the Gaza war, which some analysts believe contributed to Harris's loss.  The report also criticized the White House for assigning Harris immigration responsibilities without adequate preparation and suggested that the campaign focused too heavily on defeating Trump instead of promoting Harris's own vision. The report was released in its unedited format despite acknowledging its shortcomings and did not include specific recommendations for future elections.

articles.title: Hungary to limit PMs to eight years in office, warding off any Orbán comeback | Hungary | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Péter Magyar, leader of the Tisza party, submitted a constitutional amendment to limit prime ministers to eight years in office. The draft amendment would bar Viktor Orbán, who has served five terms as prime minister since 1998, from returning to the role.  The amendment also aims to dissolve the controversial sovereignty protection office and reclaim control of foundations that were previously controlled by loyalists of the previous government. This move is part of a broader effort by the new government to dismantle the constitution unilaterally rewritten and amended by Orbán's Fidesz party and restore democratic checks and balances. The amendment, expected to pass with the support of the Tisza party’s supermajority in parliament, will be discussed next week.

articles.title: Room for reconciliation within the AIADMK - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) and the rebel camp of the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) are attempting to reconcile after a recent trust vote where the rebels supported the government while the TVK regime voted against them.  A senior rebel leader claims efforts have been made to bring the two camps together, with mediators involved and petitions filed for disqualification proceedings. The rebel camp insists on an early general council meeting to address electoral setbacks and decision-making processes within the organization, despite not being invited to the swearing-in ceremony of the TVK regime.

articles.title: Seems PTI will now have to 'resort to agitation', says MNA after party leaders yet again denied meeting with Imran - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Ahad Ali Shah, a member of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), stated that his party would resort to agitation after being denied another meeting with former prime minister Imran Khan.  The Islamabad High Court has granted Khan twice-weekly meetings at Adiala jail, but restrictions have prevented him from meeting visitors for several weeks. The PTI submitted a list of six leaders, including Shah, for a meeting on Thursday but was denied access.  A caravan led by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi to meet Khan was stopped in Islamabad and resulted in a sit-in at Chungi No. 26.

articles.title: How Kamala Harris sank: Democrats admit 2024 went horribly wrong but have no roadmap for 2028 - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Democratic Party released a 192-page autopsy of its 2024 presidential campaign, authored by strategist Paul Rivera. The report criticizes the party's disconnect from working-class voters, weak economic messaging, cultural overreach, and organizational complacency.  It also suggests that Democrats failed to connect with Latino voters, men, rural Americans, and younger voters while failing to address issues like immigration, public safety, and inflation. However, the report notably avoids a sustained examination of President Biden's decision to seek re-election despite concerns about his age and stamina. The document was released despite criticism from Democratic National Committee chairman Ken Martin who acknowledged its shortcomings.  The party now faces internal divisions over how to address these issues and regain voter trust.

articles.title: One Nation’s rapid national expansion in disarray as ‘significant risks’ force dissolution of new branches | One Nation | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: One Nation has been forced to dissolve and re-establish its new branch network less than eight months after its ambitious rollout began due to internal inconsistencies.  The party's general manager, Kelvin Morton, issued a directive requiring all branches to comply with strict vetting processes, including non-disclosure agreements and media silence policies. This move has raised concerns about the party's commitment to free speech, as it attempts to control its grassroots movement ahead of the next election.  The party's headquarters intends to maintain tight control over branch operations and communications.

articles.title: Pauline Hanson announces Norway-inspired gas policy as she decries 25% export tax as ‘economic vandalism’ | One Nation | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: One Nation leader Pauline Hanson proposed a new policy to replace the petroleum resource rent tax (PRRT) with a royalty regime and acquire equity stakes in gas ventures.  Hanson’s proposal, which she described as “not socialist”, aims to increase returns for Australian taxpayers by co-owning new projects. The plan drew criticism from industry groups like the Minerals Council of Australia and opposition parties who argue it is not suitable for a mature industry. James Paterson, a Liberal frontbencher, called the policy "borrowed from Venezuela" while Madeleine King, the resources minister, expressed concern about government investment in an already established sector.

articles.title: CM’s appeal to kids for votes: Plea in Madras High Court seeks an inquiry by Election Commission - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: DMK, AIADMK, Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, Election Commission of India
articles.rephrased_article: A public interest litigation petition has been filed in the Madras High Court, seeking an inquiry by the Election Commission of India (ECI) into allegations of electoral malpractice during the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly elections. The petitioner, L. Vasuki, argues that Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay's appeal to children to vote for his party, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), constitutes "exploitation of minor children for electoral propaganda" and falls under the definition of corrupt practice.  The petition also cites a representation by the anti-corruption organization Arappor Iyakkam alleging that DMK and AIADMK members distributed cash to voters in certain constituencies. The court has sought responses from the ECI and CEO by May 29, 2026.

articles.title: Dublin gangland figure brings extremist views to Irish mainstream on campaign trail | Ireland | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Gerry "the monk" Hutch, a prominent gangland figure, is running as an independent candidate in the Dublin Central byelection.  His campaign has been fueled by xenophobic rhetoric and hostility towards immigrants, particularly Black immigrants and Muslims. While mainstream parties disavow racism, they have adopted tougher immigration policies. Mary Lou McDonald of Sinn Féin and Micheal Martin, the current taoiseach, have both condemned Hutch's comments on immigration. The election is being held amidst a backdrop of rising prices, housing shortages, and public discontent with the government's handling of these issues.

articles.title: D.K. Shivakumar challenges BJP leaders to travel by public transport daily - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: D.K. Shivakumar, Deputy Chief Minister of Karnataka, criticized BJP leaders for using public transport only for photoshoots in response to the Prime Minister's call for austerity measures. He challenged them to travel by public transport daily, questioning the sincerity of their actions.  He also addressed the Prime Minister's call to abstain from buying gold and expressed his commitment to visit Delhi when called upon by Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition.

articles.title: T.N. Cabinet expansion LIVE: Congress set to join Tamil Nadu’s first coalition government in decades - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay is set to expand his Cabinet with the oath of office for 23 new ministers scheduled for Thursday, May 21, 2026.  The ceremony will take place at Lok Bhavan. The Congress party, which won five seats in the alliance led by the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), is joining the coalition government. Thol. Thirumavalavan, leader of the VCK, and the IUML have been invited to join the Council of Ministers.

articles.title: Ponraj seeks anticipatory bail in two cases booked for derogatory speech against TVK women wing members - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V. Ponraj, a distinguished scientist and former advisor to the President, has filed two anticipatory bail petitions in the Madras High Court, fearing arrest by Chennai and Cuddalore police for alleged derogatory speech against women supporting C. Joseph Vijay and his party, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK).  He claims the allegations are false and politically motivated, arguing that he is a senior scientist with no flight risk and willing to cooperate with any investigation. The petitions will be heard by Justice R. Sakthivel on Thursday (May 21, 2026).

articles.title: Ponraj seeks anticipatory bail in two cases booked for derogatory speech against TVK women wing members - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V. Ponraj, a distinguished scientist and former advisor to the President, has filed two anticipatory bail petitions in the Madras High Court against arrest by Chennai and Cuddalore police for alleged derogatory speech against women supporting C. Joseph Vijay and his party, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK).  He claims the allegations are false and politically motivated, asserting that he is a senior scientist with no intention of interfering with the investigation. The petitions will be heard by Justice R. Sakthivel on Thursday (May 21, 2026).

articles.title: Chris Rabb win in Pennsylvania energises Democrats’ progressive flank | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Chris Rabb won the Pennsylvania US House primary, securing a victory that bolsters Democrats' progressive flank.  The win signifies a shift in party dynamics as Rabb, who ran on a platform of bold working-class leadership and an end to the status quo, defeated his opponents, including State Senator Sharif Street and paediatric surgeon Ala Stanford. The race is seen as a sign of hope for progressives facing challenges in primary races, particularly those critical of Washington's support for Israel.  The outcome also reflects internal strife within the Democratic party following their 2024 election loss. Rabb will likely face little opposition in the general election and represents a potential boost to Democrats' progressive wing.

articles.title: US police officers sue Trump over $1.8bn ‘anti-weaponisation’ fund | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Two US police officers, Harry Dunn and Daniel Hodges, have filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration alleging that its $1.776 billion "anti-weaponisation" fund will be used to compensate January 6th rioters. The officers argue that the fund is a form of presidential corruption and will encourage further violence by rewarding those who attacked the US Capitol.  The lawsuit seeks to dissolve the fund, claiming it allows for taxpayer money to be disbursed to participants in the attack on January 6th, 2021.

articles.title: Brexit may be back, but Britain needs to know what it wants | World news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Wes Streeting, a former health secretary and Labour party leadership candidate, recently made remarks suggesting Brexit was a "catastrophic mistake" and that the UK's future lies in the EU.  His comments reflect a deep divide within British politics regarding the impact of Brexit. While Keir Starmer, the current leader of the Labour party, has promised to reset relations with Europe, progress on closer ties remains limited. Despite economic damage caused by Brexit, there is growing support for closer UK-EU ties among both the public and European leaders. However, the UK's red lines regarding rejoining the EU or its single market remain a significant obstacle to any substantial rapprochement.

articles.title: PM busy handing out candies in Italy amid economic storm at home, says Congress - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi criticized the Narendra Modi government's economic policies, accusing it of prioritizing publicity over addressing rising inflation, unemployment, and weakening economic indicators.  Kharge highlighted the increase in average debt per Indian and wealth concentration among billionaires, while Gandhi criticized the Prime Minister's focus on foreign trips during a time of economic distress. Congress officials also pointed to the rupee's decline, falling foreign exchange reserves, and large investor outflows as evidence of government mismanagement.

articles.title: Trump endorses Ken Paxton in Texas, gambling on a challenger with baggage in a crucial race
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump endorsed Ken Paxton, Texas Attorney General, in his bid to unseat incumbent Senator John Cornyn. This move dismayed many Senate Republicans who view Paxton as a controversial figure with political baggage.  Trump's endorsement is part of a pattern of supporting challengers against Republican incumbents, and it could significantly impact the outcome of the upcoming primary election. The winner will face Democrat James Talarico in November's general election.

articles.title: Modi, Shah are traitors who are attacking the Constitution, says Rahul at Rae Bareli meet - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, leader of the Congress party, criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah, accusing them of attacking the Constitution and supporting industrialists. He also warned of an impending economic crisis, stating that it would disproportionately affect ordinary citizens while benefiting those in power.  Gandhi unveiled a statue of Veera Pasi in Rae Bareli, highlighting his party's renewed focus on the community. He further criticized the BJP government over land acquisition policies and unemployment rates, vowing to fight for the rights of the people.

articles.title: Afridi, Aleema claim shots were fired at Adiala sit-in participants - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Sohail Afridi, the Chief Minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and Aleema Khan, Imran Khan's sister, held a press conference in Islamabad where they claimed shots were fired at participants of a sit-in protesting Imran Khan's imprisonment. They alleged that the government was blocking wheat supplies to the province and that the treatment of Imran's family was unfair.  They announced plans for further protests, including one on Friday. The Tehreek Tahaffuz Ayeen-e-Pakistan (TTAP) and the PTI also announced nationwide protests against Imran Khan's imprisonment.

articles.title: TACO abroad, boss at home: Trump may be losing against China or Iran, but still controls MAGA | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump's foreign policy, particularly his handling of the Iran conflict, has led to a mixed bag of results. While he may be losing public support and facing congressional rebuke, he remains powerful within the Republican Party. Trump's tactics of intimidation have proven effective in silencing dissenters, as evidenced by the defeat of Rep. Thomas Massie, who lost his primary election after refusing to pledge unwavering loyalty. This strategy has also led to a decline in public approval ratings and fueled concerns about his ability to lead effectively.  Despite these challenges, Trump continues to hold significant sway within the Republican Party, demonstrating that loyalty trumps ideology and seniority in American politics.

articles.title: Full list of Kerala Cabinet Ministers by May 17, says Satheesan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V.D. Satheesan, the newly appointed Chief Minister of Kerala, indicated that the full list of Ministers will be presented to Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar by Sunday evening.  The swearing-in ceremony is scheduled for Monday at 10 a.m., with speculation surrounding potential ministerial appointments within the United Democratic Front (UDF). Senior Congress leader Ramesh Chennithala, reportedly disgruntled over not being chosen as Chief Minister, is rumored to be joining the Cabinet as Home Minister.  K.C. Venugopal, an aspirant for the CM's post, also met with Mr. Chennithala in conciliatory talks. The UDF is expected to finalize its ministerial appointments after discussions with all partners.

articles.title: Bidadi township: Deve Gowda announces stir against project; DKS hits back - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: H.D. Deve Gowda, former Prime Minister, launched a campaign against the proposed Bidadi township project, claiming it targets fertile agricultural land and is driven by a "land business." He accused the Siddaramaiah government of facilitating this project under the guise of urban development, drawing parallels with previous satellite township projects that were withdrawn due to public opposition. D.K. Shivakumar, Deputy Chief Minister, countered Gowda's accusations, alleging that the Kumaraswamy family amassed wealth through real estate dealings and initiated similar projects in the past.

articles.title: Average of 53% MPs attend meetings of 16 Parliamentary Standing Committees, PAC: data - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been raising concerns about the low attendance of members at parliamentary committees.  Data shows that an average of 53% of members attended meetings of 16 department-related Standing Committees and the Public Accounts Committee since their reconstitution last September, with five meetings postponed due to a lack of quorum. The data also reveals that nearly 47% of members were absent from these meetings, with better attendance observed in committees focused on Railways, Petroleum and Natural Gas, External Affairs, and Finance.  The Standing Committees discussed various important subjects including India-Sri Lanka relations, the review of the working of Border Roads Organisation (BRO), research and technology development in renewable energy, and safety and security of the diaspora during the ongoing conflict in West Asia.

articles.title: NEET paper leak row: Congress demands resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress leaders demanded the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan, the Union Education Minister, over the NEET-UG paper leak scandal.  They accused the government of a "money-making racket" involving people linked to the ruling establishment and claimed that the incident had caused immense trauma for 22 lakh students. Rahul Gandhi called for the Prime Minister's intervention, while Mallikarjun Kharge, the Congress president, alleged that the Modi government was undermining student credibility through repeated paper leaks.  Jairam Ramesh, a Congress general secretary, criticized the government's lack of action and incompetence in addressing exam reforms.

articles.title: Colorado governor faces backlash over clemency for 2020 election denier Tina Peters
articles.rephrased_article: Governor Jared Polis of Colorado faced criticism from fellow Democrats and some Republicans after commuting the prison sentence of former county clerk Tina Peters, a 2020 election denier convicted of tampering with election equipment.  Secretary of State Jena Griswold called the decision "an affront to our democracy", while President Donald Trump praised Peters' release on social media. Peters expressed remorse for her actions, but Governor Polis defended his commutation by arguing that her sentence was disproportionate for a first-time offender.

articles.title: Republican Louisiana senator in tough primary after Trump backs opponent | US Senate | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: In Louisiana's upcoming primary elections, Donald Trump's endorsement of Julia Letlow to challenge incumbent Bill Cassidy has created a significant political battle.  Cassidy, who voted to impeach the former president and later supported Robert F Kennedy Jr.'s nomination for health secretary, faces an uphill battle against Letlow and John Fleming. The changes to Louisiana's primary system, designed to favor pro-Trump candidates, have heightened Cassidy's challenges. While a runoff election is scheduled for June, Cassidy's campaign aims to secure the top two spots on Saturday and position themselves for a strong showing in the subsequent round.

articles.title: BJP protests State government’s decision to withdraw uniform rule in educational institutions - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: BJP district unit members protested against the State government's decision to withdraw uniform regulations in educational institutions, arguing that it would disrupt discipline and academic atmosphere. The protesters, including former MP Umesh Jadhav and BJP leaders Baburao Chavan, Sudha Halkai, Chandrakant Patil, and Ashok Bagli, demanded intervention from the Governor to retain the policy. They claimed uniforms promote secular values and reduce socioeconomic disparities among students.

articles.title: Lauren Boebert suggests Trump withheld funds to Colorado over prosecution of election denier | Colorado | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Lauren Boebert praised the commutation of Tina Peters' sentence, crediting President Donald Trump for the outcome. She also suggested that Peters' release could encourage Trump to stop blocking funds for a clean drinking water project in Colorado.  Boebert previously criticized colleagues for not standing up against Trump's veto of the bill, which would have provided clean water to 50,000 people.

articles.title: Remove Bandi Sanjay from Union Cabinet, Kavitha tells Modi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kalvakuntla Kavitha, president of the Telangana Rakshana Sena, urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to remove Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay Kumar from his position until the investigation and trial in the POCSO case involving his son are complete.  Kavitha expressed concern over potential conflict of interest and a perception of political influence on the investigation, arguing that public trust in the justice system could be damaged by Mr. Kumar's continued presence in office.

articles.title: Wes Streeting confirms he will stand if Labour leadership race is triggered | Wes Streeting | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Wes Streeting confirmed his intention to run for the Labour Party leadership if a contest is triggered, calling for a "proper contest" where candidates can showcase their ideas. He criticized Keir Starmer's leadership style and policies, including the winter fuel cut, arguing that Labour has lacked clarity of vision and direction since entering government.  Streeting also expressed his desire to rejoin the European Union, believing it would benefit the economy and strengthen national defense.

articles.title: How Thomas Massie came to represent Republican dissent in age of Trump | Government News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Congressman Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican known for his dissenting views on foreign policy and military aid to Israel, is facing a tough re-election bid against Ed Gallrein.  Massie has consistently voted against policies favored by the Trump administration, including tax bills and military interventions abroad. He has also been vocal in opposing unconditional US military aid to Israel. Pro-Israel groups have poured money into Gallrein's campaign, while Massie argues that this spending is a reflection of a foreign lobby attempting to influence elections. The outcome of the race could signal broader fault lines within the Republican base regarding foreign policy and support for Israel.

articles.title: Law Minister Tarar sees ‘no indication’ of 28th amendment for now - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar stated that the 28th Constitutional Amendment would require consultation with coalition partners and consensus on all issues. He clarified that constitutional amendments cannot be implemented without this process, noting ongoing discussions about population control, Hazara and Saraiki provinces, and local government systems.  PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari stated that the PPP has not been contacted by the government regarding a constitutional amendment and emphasized their role in previous amendments expanding provincial representation.

articles.title: Andalucíans to vote in election seen as gauge of Spain’s wider political change | Spain | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The upcoming election in Andalucía, Spain's most populous region, is expected to deliver an absolute majority for the conservative People’s Party (PP) and further weaken the Socialists. Juan Manuel Moreno Bonilla, the PP regional president, seeks to capitalize on scandals surrounding Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and his administration.  The PP aims to portray the election as a referendum on Sánchez's leadership, while Vox is expected to gain seats. The outcome will have implications for Spain's upcoming general election next year.

articles.title: KTR asks party leaders and BLAs to be alert during SIR - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K.T. Rama Rao, working president of the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS), met with Assembly Constituency in-charges to discuss electoral roll revisions and membership drives. He cautioned against potential voter suppression by Congress and BJP.  He urged party members to protect voters' rights and expose the opposing parties' policies. At a separate meeting with Sanathnagar constituency activists, KTR stated that the BJP has minimal presence in the state and their Lok Sabha election performance was an anomaly.

articles.title: Ultra-Orthodox conscription dispute pushes Israeli government to brink | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Israeli government is facing a crisis due to the withdrawal of support from ultra-Orthodox parties, who are demanding an exemption from military conscription. The coalition has called for an early election following continued fractures over the issue.  Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government is struggling to address the demands of the ultra-Orthodox parties, with their spiritual leader calling for the dissolution of the Knesset. This situation has prompted calls for sanctions on those who refuse conscription and a potential end to benefits for religious students whose families rely on them. The Israeli military argues that recruiting ultra-Orthodox men is crucial for sustaining its operations in the region.

articles.title: T.N. Cabinet portfolios: CM Vijay to hold Home; Finance for Sengottaiyan; Aadhav Arjuna gets PWD - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, has announced the portfolios for his cabinet members. Vijay will oversee key departments including Home, Police, and IAS/IPS officers.  N. Anand, the deputy chief minister, will handle Rural Development and Water Resources. Other ministers have been assigned specific responsibilities in areas such as health, education, finance, and energy. The Governor has approved the recommendations.

articles.title: SIR in Telangana: Draft electoral rolls to have names of electors whose Enumeration Forms are received - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Electoral Registration Officers (ERO) in Telangana will publish draft electoral rolls on July 31, 2026, including names of all electors whose Enumeration Forms were received.  Following this, EROs will issue notices to individuals who cannot be linked or have discrepancies in their linking with the previous revision's electoral rolls. This is part of a Special Intensive Revision (SIR) conducted for the first time since 2002 when Telangana was part of united Andhra Pradesh.

articles.title: Manoj Jarange warns of fresh agitation over Maratha quota issue from May 30 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Manoj Jarange, a Maratha quota activist, announced an indefinite hunger strike beginning May 30th over the Maharashtra government's failure to distribute Kunbi caste certificates and implement other demands.  Jarange demanded the dissolution of the Maratha quota sub-committee and urged for a separate ministry for the Maratha and Kunbi communities. He also criticized the state government for halting the issuance of Kunbi caste certificates, claiming that officials have been instructed not to issue them. Devendra Fadnavis, the Chief Minister of Maharashtra, has been accused by Jarange of being responsible for these actions.

articles.title: Russia’s Putin to visit China following Trump’s trip | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Vladimir Putin will visit China from May 19 to 20, the Kremlin announced. The trip is timed to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the Treaty of Good-Neighborliness and Friendly Cooperation signed in 2001 between the two countries.  Putin will meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and discuss economic and trade cooperation. This visit follows Donald Trump’s departure from China after his first presidential trip to Beijing in almost a decade, during which he and Xi Jinping discussed several broad trade deals but made little public progress on key sticking points related to Taiwan or the US-Israel war on Iran.

articles.title: Stateside with Kai and Carter: Stacey Abrams on why gutting of the US Voting Rights Act is ‘evil’ – podcast | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US Supreme Court ruled in *Louisiana v.
